sites.name: Shackleton–de Gerlache Connecting Ridge
sites.note: Best-lit point Earthset found within 800 m of the highly illuminated site reported by Mazarico et al. 2011 (89.45°S 222.69°E). Moving just 80 m changes long-term sunlight from ~64% to ~86%.

sites.name: Malapert Massif (summit area)
sites.note: Illustrative point inside the Artemis III "Malapert Massif" candidate region; NASA has not published site coordinates.
sites.src: LOLA topography (summit), region name from NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024)

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.note: IAU feature coordinates; Artemis III candidate regions "Mons Mouton" and "Mons Mouton Plateau" lie on this mountain.

sites.name: IM-2 Athena (CLPS, 2025)
sites.note: Intuitive Machines IM-2, landed 6 Mar 2025 on Mons Mouton; came to rest on its side in a shadowed crater.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (CLPS, 2024)
sites.note: Intuitive Machines IM-1, landed 22 Feb 2024 near Malapert A.

sites.name: Shackleton Crater floor (PSR)
sites.note: Permanently shadowed region: the Sun never clears the rim. Included as a contrast case.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (ISRO, 2023)
sites.note: ISRO Chandrayaan-3, landed 23 Aug 2023 ("Shiv Shakti Point").

sites.name: Blue Ghost M1 (CLPS, 2025)
sites.note: Firefly Blue Ghost Mission 1, Mare Crisium, landed 2 Mar 2025 (target coordinates).

sites.name: SLIM (JAXA, 2024)
sites.note: JAXA Smart Lander for Investigating Moon, near Shioli crater.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 (CNSA, 2019) — far side
sites.note: Far side: Earth never rises here, so direct-to-Earth communication is impossible.

sites.name: Chang'e 6 (CNSA, 2024) — far side
sites.note: Far side sample return, Apollo basin.
